### When the Spiritual Relationship Hurts

If a spiritual teacher you trusted betrayed you, even sitting down to meditate can feel like it belongs to them now. Kids quit piano over one bad teacher, and this is way worse. But if you let an abuser control your appreciation of life, then you've given them an unearned win.

What they have to carry, in meaning, not in anyone's wording: the love you can feel for a dog is real love; some readers also know a love of a different size altogether, in prayer or meditation or with God, and it shouldn't be lumped in with the dog or turned into a thought experiment about a friend; if you have that, use as much of it as you can honestly reach today, and let your little one into it; whatever they do with it (going numb, saying "Bullshit") is what you listen to next, instead of adding more of the spiritual practice on top, which doesn't reach them.
- Every version so far has kept the same order: the claim, the bigger love as a contrast, the instruction, the list of reactions, then the moral about not adding more on top. In its section Pangram flags the instruction sentence every time ("Get as close to it as you really can right now, and bring your little one in with you."; "If you've known that bigger love, get as close to it as you really can right now, without shrinking it down to a thought experiment about a friend, and bring your little one in with you."). Don't keep that order or rebuild that sentence. Say it the way the narrator would say it out loud to a reader who prays or meditates. If you use the objection (that this isn't the same as loving a dog), give it its own plain sentence.
- No pointer to anything sections back (the food bank, or any earlier section). The dog is fine: it's this h2's own first paragraph.

guide_passage:
Ask God for a Loan
Ordinary love and profound spiritual love are both real forms of love, but I don’t want to flatten them into the same experience. Caring about a friend, feeding somebody who is hungry, protecting a child, or wanting an animal to be comfortable may give you exactly the pathway you need to begin. That is real love.
But some people have also experienced a kind of love that feels radically different in depth or scale: divine love, universal love, a heart opening, the love encountered in prayer or meditation, or something revealed in a spiritual or mystical experience. If you already know that territory, don’t reduce it to a thought experiment about how you would treat a friend.
Find whatever access to that love is genuinely available now. Then bring the younger self into the same field.
Don’t force it. If the child goes numb, distrusts the love, feels threatened by it, or says, “Bullshit,” that reaction becomes the pl/ork. Listen to it. The answer is not to pour more spirituality on top.
This is the feast problem. You can have an enormous spiritual feast upstairs while the child is still starving downstairs. Spiritual integration means some of what you have actually reaches them.
